title: Precision retry contracts for hedged requests and SLO-driven backoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a single, precise contract that standardizes retry/timeout/backoff semantics across Redwood services and SDKs with explicit hedged-request semantics and SLO-aligned retry budgets. Current behavior varies by service: SDKs do client-side retries with inconsistent idempotency expectations, runtime hedging is ad-hoc, and circuit breaker integration differs by region. This ticket defines the contract (server headers, client SDK API, idempotency key format, hedged request TTLs, and SLO-based budgets), implements SDK changes for node/python/go, updates runtime to expose hedging metadata, and adds dashboards and runbooks to validate behavior in multi-region failover scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: A1: SDKs expose a single RetryPolicy object supporting: max_attempts, base_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, jitter_strategy, hedged_enabled(boolean), hedged_parallelism(int), and idempotency_key propagation
A2: Server runtime accepts and returns standardized headers: X-Redwood-Idempotency, X-Redwood-Retry-After, X-Redwood-Hedge-Outcome, and documents semantics
A3: Hedged requests are limited by a per-tenant SLO-aligned retry budget; an opt-in per-route override is supported in Console
A4: Circuit breaker and load-shed signals interoperate: when breakers open, clients receive 429 with Retry-After; SDK honors and atomically updates local budget stats

A5: Dashboards show retries_per_request, hedged_success_rate, retries_exhausted, per-region_failover_count, and SLO impact; alerts triggered when hedged_success_rate drops >10% or retries_per_request > 3 for 5m
A6: Migration guide and runbook exist; internal canary rollout across 10% traffic for 2 days followed by progressive increase
work_items: W1: Draft and review the contract doc (this ticket) with infra, runtime, SDK, and product
W2: Implement header parsing and hedging metadata emission in runtime v1.20
W3: Add RetryPolicy type to NodeJS/Python/Go SDKs with backward-compatible defaults
W4: Implement client-side idempotency key generator and opt-in propagation
W5: Wire circuit-breaker state to API gateway so opened breakers return 429 + Retry-After
W6: Add metrics and trace attributes: retry_count, hedge_attempts, hedge_outcomes, idempotency_conflicts
W7: Create dashboards and PagerDuty runbook entries for hedging/regression alerts
W8: Execute staged rollout and collect regression/eval prompts to validate quality trade-offs
design_decisions: D1: Idempotency key is 128-bit UUID v4 encoded as hex with optional route-prefix: <route>::<uuid> to allow per-endpoint uniqueness and simple collision tracing

D2: Hedged requests: default hedged_enabled=false. When true, hedged_parallelism=2 by default. Hedged attempts must attach identical idempotency_key and a Hedged-At timestamp header to allow server-side duplicate suppression

D3: SLO-aligned retry budget: each tenant has a token bucket derived from historical QPS and target error budget (SLO_error_budget). SDK consumes tokens before issuing retries/hedges; when depleted, SDK falls back to best-effort single attempt or surface to app via callback

D4: Backoff semantics: exponential with full-jitter per AWS guidance, base_backoff_ms and max_backoff_ms enforced; hedged attempts are triggered by time offset (hedge_delay_ms) not by failed attempt completion
D5: Circuit breaker contract: breaker emits open state via X-Redwood-Breaker-State and client SDKs must stop retries and surface errors immediately when breaker_open=true for the route

D6: Server-side deduplication: runtime will use idempotency key + request fingerprint to detect duplicates for up to 60s (configurable per-route), but long-running idempotency up to configurable TTL supported for stateful endpoints

D7: Multi-region failover: routing policy will set X-Redwood-Region-Primary and X-Redwood-Region-Fallback headers; hedging may be used across regions only when tenant has cross-region failover enabled and SLO budget allows
rollout_plan: R1: Merge contract doc and runtime changes to canary cluster; run synthetic load harness against slow-path to validate hedging semantics
R2: Release SDK patch versions behind feature flag 'precision-retries' and set default to off for 30% of orgs; incrementally enable for internal customers
R3: 10% traffic canary for 48h with detailed metrics collection (latency p50/p95/p99, cost delta, hedged_success_rate, customer-visible error rate)
R4: If metrics stable, progressively increase to 50% then 100% over 7 days; if regressions > 2x error budget, rollback and run postmortem
R5: Publish migration guide in Console docs and run a webinar for Solutions/SEs to explain idempotency key usage and SDK changes
metrics_and_alerting: M1: retries_per_request (histogram) - alert if mean > 1.5 over 5m for a tenant with >100rps
M2: hedged_success_rate by route - alert if drop >10% vs baseline for 15m
M3: idempotency_conflict_rate - monitor; alert if >0.1% sustained for 30m
M4: circuit_open_ratio per region - alert if any region has open_ratio > 0.05 for 10m
M5: cost_delta_tokens - estimate additional GPU inference tokens from hedging; warn product if weekly cost growth > 5%
M6: per-tenant retry_budget_consumption (tokens/sec) - alert when a tenant exhausts budget repeatedly
test_plan: T1: Unit tests for SDK RetryPolicy serialization, idempotency key propagation, and header round-trip
T2: Integration tests: simulate transient 500 errors and verify SDK uses backoff and hedged attempts per policy
T3: Chaos tests: blackout primary region, verify hedged cross-region failover triggers when enabled and that duplicates are suppressed
T4: Load test: measure p95/p99 under hedging vs no-hedging for representative prompt sizes; assert cost impact within acceptable bounds
T5: Fuzz tests to ensure idempotency dedupe does not incorrectly drop distinct requests
